notes: Origin: one of the twelve root cases of the retired obstructed corpus.
Old title: "Joint-loop equivalence: tc_left vs all_paths_via_even_odd (non-linear, naive)" (kind: equiv-pair; algorithm: naive).

Prior classification and evidence in the retired corpus: valid, by a hand-written Lean kernel certificate (direct Lean kernel proof that naive left-recursive transitive closure and the nonlinear even/odd path program have the same fixed point; no external FOL assumptions). The retired corpus records this case among the twelve valid, conjecturally FO-obstructed cases (no archived Vampire refutation for this particular case). That kernel certificate is not carried into this corpus; the classification here is unknown until re-certified.

The command is not hand-authored: `Fidelity/Example0136.lean` states the two Datalog programs written for this case, compiles each with `Datalog.WhielCompiler.Naive`, writes the two compiled commands one after the other, renames the generated snapshots to the auxiliary input names `X_aux`, and proves the result equal to `inputCmd` by `decide +kernel`; the same module fixes `inputPre` and `inputPost` and pins the single loop `Hoare.preprocess` computes from the sequence. The two programs are independent, so the preprocessor merges them into the flag-free guarded parallel form.

The retired file's loop iterated destructively, carrying a second copy `SX` of each relation and stepping the immediate-consequence operator from the empty relation; the compiled form accumulates, `T := T ∪ T_P(T)`, and reaches the same least fixpoint. The retired postcondition `TX = TcY` was stated over those previous-round copies, which equal the fixpoints at loop exit; the same equality is stated here over the compiled output relations, so the triple says the same thing. The schema loses the copies `SX`, `SaY`, `SbY`, `ScY` and gains the compiler's snapshots `TX_aux`, `TaY_aux`, `TbY_aux`, `TcY_aux`. The precondition `true` is unchanged, and the expected verdict stays valid.
title: Right-linear transitive closure versus the non-linear odd/even path program (two compiled loops)
explanation: The command runs two independently compiled Datalog programs in sequence — a right-linear transitive-closure program producing TX, and a non-linear even/odd program producing TaY, TbY and their union TcY — merged by the preprocessor into a single verified loop. The postcondition TX=TcY is an equivalence claim: the ordinary transitive closure of E equals the union of the even-length and odd-length path relations, since every nonempty path has odd or even length.
preInWords: The precondition is simply true, imposing no constraint on the input relations.
postInWords: The postcondition asserts that the transitive closure TX computed by the first program equals TcY, the union of even- and odd-length paths computed by the second.

datalog.text:
TaY(x1, y1) :- E(x1, z1), E(z1, y1).
TaY(x1, y1) :- TaY(x1, z1), TaY(z1, y1).
TaY(x1, y1) :- TbY(x1, z1), TbY(z1, y1).
TbY(x1, y1) :- E(x1, y1).
TbY(x1, y1) :- TbY(x1, z1), TaY(z1, y1).
TbY(x1, y1) :- TaY(x1, z1), TbY(z1, y1).
TcY(x1, y1) :- TaY(x1, y1).
TcY(x1, y1) :- TbY(x1, y1).
